memory_candidates.content: In this repo's typst/ book, scripts/typst-sync-check.sh Check 1 (backtick-span resolution) scans // comments as well as prose, so illustrative Lean-syntax spans left in editorial TODO comments (e.g. `structure ... where`, `name : Type`) can silently fail the sync gate. The sanctioned remedy is a new category in typst/sync-check-whitelist.txt, following the existing 'generic Lean tooling illustrations' pattern, never editing the commented-out prose itself if the file is off-limits.

Typst technique for supplement-aware #show ref on level-1 headings: rather than hardcoding a fixed supplement string (e.g. "Chapter") and a fixed numbering pattern in a document-wide show:ref rule, read the heading element's own el.supplement and el.numbering dynamically (link(it.target)[#el.supplement~#numbering(el.numbering, ..counter(heading).at(el.location()))]), guarded by `if el.numbering == none`. This lets one rule correctly render multiple heading kinds (chapters numbered "1", appendices numbered "A") that each set their own local supplement/numbering via #show heading.where(level:1): set heading(...) overrides, without branching on file or heading level.

In BimodalLogic's FormalSystem/Automation/Tactics/Search.lean, both `Axiom` and `DerivationTree` are Type-valued (not Prop-valued) -- there is no Prop/Type mismatch between them, contrary to docstrings that claimed one. The authoritative, correct explanation for why Aesop-style automation doesn't work on DerivationTree goals (and why the hand-written TacticM search exists) lives in Boneyard/RetiredTactics/README.md's write-up of the retired TMLogic Aesop rule set: Aesop's reconstruction targets Prop-valued goals (leaning on proof irrelevance), while DerivationTree goals are Type-valued data where the specific term matters.
